scope: Corollary 9.3 of the manuscript “A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function” (preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 021 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f80267eebc82a9b8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 59-60. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the compact range and ε > 0. For every prescribed positive ρ, the inverse exception parameter and then the variance exception parameter can be chosen so that, for a fixed Cs independent of sufficiently small fixed ξ, the following holds for all sufficiently large z. Consider the actual included regular compact endpoints covered by the full boxes of 59 Theorem 7.2. Except for a set of these endpoints of total harmonic mass at most ρB−2, every such bad endpoint |Nd/µd − 1| > ε has a witnessing candidate and a rational on that candidate’s fixed list for which the parent is structured, the isolated prime aligns, and Dqf,E ≤ wCs , |C0|/R ≤ wCs . (9.23) For each such endpoint all its prime factors with exponent x(t) > Cs align to this same rational, including the isolated prime. The rational satisfies the global bounds D ≤ wCs , |A| ≤ Y wCs+2 . (9.24) The enlarged full boxes are used only to dominate measure: the assertion concerns the actual included endpoints, rather than every tuple in those enlarged boxes. The exceptional mass can be bounded before choosing ξ; only the eventual threshold on z is allowed to depend on fixed ξ.
